      "body": "Implements the design resolved by [Design stable Bash command interfaces for homelab-iac](https://github.com/faviann/homelab-iac/issues/189). Every decision below traces to a closed ticket on that map; the consolidated matrix is in [#198's resolution](https://github.com/faviann/homelab-iac/issues/198#issuecomment-5418235197).

## Problem Statement

Getting this repository to do anything requires knowing raw `uv` incantations. Tracked guidance teaches 25 distinct raw command shapes across 36 lines in seven files, and the wider tree carries 103 more. There are two Bash commands — `./run.sh` and `./validate.sh` — and they own only two operations between them. Everything else is a raw command copied out of a README.

That costs three different people three different ways.

**An operator** cannot tell which commands are safe. `./run.sh` serializes lifecycle mutation behind a lock; the raw provisioning command printed in `README.md` does the same work with no lock at all. Connectivity, credential, and API diagnostics are three separate raw playbook invocations with overlapping content and no shared vocabulary, and one of them always exits `0` even when a host is unreachable.

**An agent** is told by `AGENTS.md` to run Ansible tools through `uv run --locked <tool>` — and then handed a merged-variable debugging command that prints 73 vault-derived lines. That command is the largest secret-disclosure surface in the tracked guidance, and it is documented as the way to debug. Agents also cannot distinguish an approved raw command from one that happens to appear in a document.

**A contributor** has one feedback command, `./validate.sh`, which runs everything and takes minutes. Every targeted alternative — lint alone, one launcher, one test file — is a raw command they must learn. Worse, `./validate.sh` is described as deterministic and non-live, and it is neither: it cannot start without the machine-local vault passphrase, 34 of its 44 direct-Ansible regression tests inherit the real inventory and are kept off the network only by a hand-written `connection: local` in each fixture, and one unit test decrypts the vault and sends a real bearer token to the live Authentik API on every real workstation.

The through-line: the command surface is an accident of history rather than a designed interface, so safety properties are unenforceable, secrets leak through documented paths, and nobody can tell what they are allowed to run.

## Solution

Six purpose-named Bash commands become the entire supported interface, for contributors, operators, and agents alike.

| Command | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `./setup.sh` | Guided workstation setup, plus targeted controller reconciliation |
| `./vault.sh` | Vault configuration, editing, verification, key transfer, passphrase rotation |
| `./validate.sh` | Comprehensive non-live handoff validation, plus targeted feedback |
| `./inspect.sh` | Read-only managed-host diagnostics and inventory observation |
| `./recover.sh` | Narrow state-restoring recovery |
| `./run.sh` | Full, provision-only, and configure-only lifecycle execution |

Every raw command that gains an owner is **removed** from tracked guidance rather than kept as a compatibility shim — a raw form left in a document is the form the next agent copies. Five raw commands survive as recorded standing permissions, each carrying its trigger, audience, scope, boundary, and escalation condition.

Three properties become true that are only claimed today:

- **`./validate.sh` needs no machine-local secret.** It exports a fixture inventory and fixture passphrase once for its whole run, so the non-live boundary is a property of the command rather than a convention held up by per-fixture discipline.
- **No supported operation prints a secret.** The merged-variable command survives as `./inspect.sh vars` and prints **masked values** — letters as `a`, digits as `9`, every other character literal, whitespace as a visible token — so the fault class this repository actually suffers from stays diagnosable while the secret does not print.
- **Read-only live operations cannot observe state mid-transition.** The lifecycle lock splits into shared and exclusive classes, so a diagnostic takes a shared lock and a lifecycle run takes an exclusive one.

Nine tests reachable from `./validate.sh` enforce the result, and one new document, `docs/command-policy.md`, holds the policy that `AGENTS.md` is too small to carry.

## User Stories

### Discovering and running commands

1. As a contributor, I want six purpose-named commands rather than 25 raw shapes, so that I can find the operation I need without reading a README first.
2. As a contributor, I want every command to answer `--help` with its operations, so that I can discover the interface from the terminal.
3. As a contributor, I want `./run.sh`, `./validate.sh`, and `./setup.sh` to have safe no-argument defaults, so that the common case needs no arguments.
4. As an operator, I want `./vault.sh`, `./inspect.sh`, and `./recover.sh` to require an explicit operation, so that I never trigger a consequential default by typing a bare command.
5. As a contributor, I want every command to reject an unknown operation or option with a distinct exit status, so that a typo fails loudly instead of being silently ignored.
6. As an agent, I want one documented exit convention across all six commands, so that I can branch on the outcome without special-casing each script.
7. As an operator, I want lock contention to return a status distinct from failure, so that "someone else is deploying" and "the deploy failed" are not the same signal to a script.
8. As an operator, I want a command that cannot take its lock to stop immediately and name the holder, so that I never mistake a wait for a hang during a five-to-ten-minute run.

### Lifecycle execution

9. As an operator, I want `./run.sh` to keep running the **full lifecycle** by default, so that the command I already use does not change meaning.
10. As an operator, I want `./run.sh provision` and `./run.sh configure` to run the **provision-only lifecycle** and **configure-only lifecycle**, so that lifecycle slices have first-class names.
11. As an operator, I want `--stack <name>` instead of an `-e` variable override, so that selecting one stack cannot be confused with defeating a guard.
12. As an operator, I want `--include-controller` instead of an `-e` variable override, so that the single most dangerous flag in the repository has a name that says what it does.
13. As an operator, I want `--limit` to keep Ansible's own grammar — groups, patterns, comma lists, `!` exclusion — so that `--limit cap_docker` keeps working and I learn no second syntax.
14. As an operator, I want every other Ansible argument to move behind `--`, so that low-level passthrough is visibly separate from the supported grammar.
15. As an operator, I want passthrough to be unable to change target selection, **lifecycle intent**, the lock, or wrapper enforcement, so that the escape hatch cannot defeat the safety boundary.
16. As an operator, I want `./run.sh --check` to take a shared rather than exclusive lock, so that a dry run does not block a colleague's diagnostic.

### Diagnostics and inspection

17. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh credentials` to walk the Proxmox API credential and permission ladder, so that one command tells me whether my token works and how far it reaches.
18. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh connectivity` to report SSH reachability of the LXCs, so that I can check the fleet without a raw ad-hoc module call.
19. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh connectivity` to exit non-zero when a target is unreachable, so that I can use it from a script — today's playbook always exits `0`.
20. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh containers` to list the LXCs the Proxmox node actually has, so that I can see a VMID conflict with a container no **LXC identity reservation** covers.
21. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh plan` to run **LXC contract compilation**, **fleet preflight**, **LXC observation**, and produce an **LXC lifecycle plan** per target without executing anything, so that I can see every detected problem before committing to a run.
22. As an agent, I want `./inspect.sh vars <host>` to show merged inventory variables with vault-derived values masked, so that I can debug variable precedence without putting a secret in a transcript.
23. As an agent, I want the mask to preserve every non-alphanumeric character and render whitespace visibly, so that I can diagnose a trailing space or an unescaped `$` — the faults this repository actually hits.
24. As a maintainer, I want the mask to collapse case, so that masked output reaching a pull request does not hand an attacker a wordlist hint.
25. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh vars --graph` to show the group membership tree, so that I can read inventory structure without a raw command.
26. As an operator, I want `./inspect.sh vars` to take no lock, so that a running deploy does not make a local inventory read fail.
27. As an operator, I want the read-only inspect operations to take a shared lock, so that they cannot observe managed-host state part-way through a mutation.

### Recovery

28. As an operator, I want `./recover.sh ssh-keys` to perform **manual SSH recovery**, so that restoring access has a named command rather than a raw playbook invocation.
29. As an operator, I want `./recover.sh ssh-keys` to work when unrelated desired state is invalid, so that ADR-0002's independent recovery guarantee survives the new interface.
30. As an operator, I want `./recover.sh ssh-keys` to establish Proxmox host access itself, so that the manual "run the bootstrap tags first" prerequisite disappears.
31. As an operator, I want `./recover.sh` to require an explicit operation and take an exclusive lock, so that a state-changing recovery is never accidental and never concurrent with a lifecycle run.

### Setup and bootstrap

32. As a contributor on a fresh machine, I want `./setup.sh` with no arguments to walk me through workstation setup, so that the guided path is unchanged.
33. As an agent in a fresh worktree, I want `./setup.sh sync` to materialize the locked controller environment non-interactively, so that I do not run interactive credential onboarding to get three install steps.
34. As an agent in a fresh worktree, I want `./setup.sh bootstrap` to reconcile collections, roles, and the controller SSH key non-interactively, so that a new worktree reaches a runnable state with one documented command.
35. As a contributor, I want `./setup.sh bootstrap` to create the controller SSH key only when absent, so that it never rotates a key the fleet already trusts.
36. As a contributor, I want `./setup.sh sync` and `bootstrap` to remain independent repair paths, so that I can fix one layer without re-running the other.
37. As a contributor, I want guided setup to leave an existing encrypted vault untouched, so that re-running setup is never destructive.

### Vault

38. As an operator, I want `./vault.sh configure` to prompt through a TTY for Proxmox credentials, so that secrets never pass through arguments or environment variables.
39. As an operator, I want reconfiguration to preserve every unrelated vault key, so that updating credentials cannot silently drop another stack's secret.
40. As an operator, I want `./vault.sh edit` to open the whole encrypted vault in my editor, so that general editing has one obvious path.
41. As an agent, I want `./vault.sh check` to verify the vault non-disclosingly — header, passphrase file existence and permissions, decryptability, structure, required keys present and non-placeholder — so that I can confirm the vault is sound without seeing a value.
42. As an agent, I want `./vault.sh set <key> --from-file <path>` to move a secret into the vault without reading it, so that I can perform a requested credential transfer without the secret entering my transcript.
43. As an operator, I want `--create` and `--replace` to be explicit and mutually exclusive, so that a transfer cannot silently overwrite or silently create.
44. As an operator, I want the source file for a transfer to be rejected unless it is a current-user-owned regular file with no group or world permissions, so that a transfer cannot pick up a world-readable or symlinked secret.
45. As an operator, I want `./vault.sh rotate` to keep its confirmation, tmpfs handling, rekey-before-publish ordering, ciphertext backup, verification, and rollback behaviour, so that passphrase rotation loses none of its existing safety.
46. As an agent, I want `./vault.sh rotate --dry-run` to rehearse on throwaway copies, so that I can verify rotation logic without touching the real vault, Bitwarden, or the live passphrase.
47. As an operator, I want no supported operation that prints decrypted vault contents, so that the disclosure path documented today simply ceases to exist.
48. As an operator, I want vault plaintext to exist only in a mode-700 tmpfs workspace and never at the tracked vault path, so that an interrupted operation cannot leave plaintext on disk.
49. As an operator, I want a failed vault mutation to leave the original file untouched, so that a partial write cannot corrupt the vault.

### Targeted feedback

50. As a contributor, I want `./validate.sh` with no arguments to remain the comprehensive handoff command, so that the required pre-handoff step does not change.
51. As a contributor, I want `./validate.sh lint` for repo-wide lint alone, so that I get fast style feedback while iterating.
52. As a contributor, I want `./validate.sh lifecycle` for the fast lifecycle regression path, so that I get lifecycle feedback in about a minute and a half instead of six.
53. As a contributor, I want `--full`, `--only <launcher.py>` (repeatable), and `--fail-fast` on that operation, so that every selection mode the runner already supports has a supported command form.
54. As a contributor, I want `./validate.sh tests [<target>…]` to select test files or node ids, so that I can iterate on one test without learning a raw invocation.
55. As a contributor, I want test targets outside the test tree rejected as invalid usage, so that the operation cannot become a general test runner.
56. As a stack maintainer, I want `./validate.sh stack <path>` to validate one **stack update policy**, so that per-stack policy checking has a supported command.
57. As a developer integrating with stack tooling, I want `./validate.sh stack` to emit schema-versioned JSON on stdout with diagnostics on stderr, so that later image-update planning can consume it as a stable contract.
58. As a contributor,…18090 tokens truncated…lper and the 39 migrations are one change — the suite is broken in between.*

**5 — `./validate.sh` operations.** Add `lint`, `lifecycle`, `tests`, `stack`. Rewrite `test_validate_command.py`'s exact-argv pinning into test 1's grammar coverage.
*Touches `validate.sh` again after change 4; kept separate because 4 is a whole-run property and 5 is argument parsing.*

**6 — `./vault.sh` and `./setup.sh`.** Create `vault.sh` with `configure`, `edit`, `check`, `set`, `rotate [--dry-run]`. Delete `configure-vault.sh` and `rotate-vault-passphrase.sh` outright — no shim. Add `setup.sh sync` and `setup.sh bootstrap`; rewrite its echoed follow-ups. **Test 9 lands here.**

**7 — `./inspect.sh vars` and the mask.** The pure mask function, the `vault_*` derivation, the `--graph` operation. **Test 8 lands here. ADR: the masked value.**
*Kept separate from change 3 because of its own scope tripwire and ADR.*

**8 — Documentation and text migration.** All 23 files (#197's 11 plus this ticket's 12), the runtime and comment text, `docs/command-policy.md` created and linked from `AGENTS.md` and `README.md`, the `AGENTS.md` non-negotiable replaced. **Test 6 lands here.**
*Constraint 3: last, because test 6 fails until every command it names exists.*

**The `AGENTS.md` non-negotiable becomes:**

> Use the repository's Bash commands. Do not invoke Ansible, `uv`, or `pytest` directly. `docs/command-policy.md` gives the approved exceptions.

---

## 8. `docs/command-policy.md`

The new file carries: the six-command vocabulary and grammar; the rule for a seventh command; #196's internal-call rule; the five standing-permission records with their #192 fields; test 6's allowlist; the machine-local scope of the lock (#174); the CI fact (#200); and the recorded boundaries —

- guards run only under `./validate.sh`;
- a secret shorter than 8 characters can print when a different variable contains it;
- a secret written into a plain `group_vars` file is not masked;
- a vault key without the `vault_` prefix is not masked by rule 1;
- a test run under plain `pytest` does not inherit the fixture environment;
- a localhost-only playbook that delegates to the Proxmox host without importing L3 is not detected as live.

`AGENTS.md` is 119 lines and read in full every session; five permission records with six fields each would roughly double it with material an agent needs only when about to do something unusual. It keeps a Command Reference table rewritten to the six commands, and its long-running output discipline block with the live `inspect.sh` operations added.

---

## 9. ADRs

Three, each landing with its change:

1. **The masked value** (change 7) — an agent may print a derivative of a secret; argued both ways (closed flag list versus open mask, case preserved versus collapsed); hard to reverse once masked output has reached transcripts and pull requests. It also amends a security rule set by #192.
2. **Enforcing the non-live boundary in the validation command** (change 4) — a validation command silently overrides Ansible's inventory and vault password, and nothing in the 39 test files shows it.
3. **The shared/exclusive lock split** (change 3) — surprising that a read-only command takes a lock at all; a real trade-off (`--wait` rejected, check mode audited rather than trusted); hard to reverse once `inspect.sh` and `recover.sh` depend on it. It amends ADR-0001's linear-execution model and should be findable beside it.

---

- **#175 is not satisfied.** The fixture environment makes the suite *non-live*; it does not make it *offline*. `workstation_persistent_home_disabled.yml`, `workstation_first_login_setup_contract.yml`, and `workstation_baseline_github_keys_test.yml` still reach `github.com` when their `-e` overrides are dropped. #195 stated the boundary as no-managed-host precisely so this would not be read as an offline guarantee.

## Owed validation and phase ownership

- **Primary checkpoint / initial-gate path:** rerun only invalidated focused checks after readiness corrections and populate direct evidence for every frozen member not already settled by qualifying exact-candidate evidence.
- **Gate:** fresh Standards, Spec, and cumulative closure judgments consume the complete frozen surface and qualifying raw evidence; they do not execute a full regression merely because the gate began.
- **Remediation:** only focused checks and frozen members invalidated by an accepted corrective batch; no full regression.
- **Closeout:** run the complete no-argument `./validate.sh` under a fresh empty `HOME` with no machine-local vault passphrase, satisfying criteria 4 and 9 when green; run `git diff --check`. Reuse that exact qualifying full-run evidence rather than executing `./validate.sh` twice.

The repository-required full handoff command is owned by Closeout. It is not an implementation-completion prerequisite and must not be pre-produced for reuse.
# Validation evidence reuse

Apply this policy whenever an implementation, readiness, Standards, Spec, or
closure context produces or adjudicates validation evidence. The frozen
Validation-surface manifest remains the complete population of direct evidence
the accepted candidate owes; this policy decides whether qualifying evidence
for a listed member must be executed again. It owns evidence identity,
sufficiency, invalidation, and reuse; it does not decide the workflow phase in
which evidence is executed. The selected workflow owns that timing, and this
policy applies when the owning phase is reached.

## Qualifying evidence

Candidate identity names the exact repository and all candidate-controlled
content under assessment. Include the base only when the validation depends on
the base or diff. Validation identity names the exact command, arguments,
working directory, and other check-defining inputs. Reusable-evidence identity
combines that Candidate identity and Validation identity with every relevant
environment, toolchain, external-input, and artifact identity whose change
could affect the result.

Reusable validation evidence supplies recoverable source provenance, execution
status, and inspectable raw output or a result artifact. A prior participant's
pass conclusion is not evidence. Every reviewer still makes a fresh Independent
judgment from the candidate, contract, and raw evidence without inheriting
prior conclusions, adjudications, or dispositions. Validity depends on identity
and provenance, not producer role.

Wave 1 uses a conservative exact-candidate rule. A committed HEAD qualifies
when the required worktree state is proven clean. Evidence from an uncommitted
state qualifies only when its content identity was deterministically captured
and proven identical to the reviewed candidate.

Evidence remains valid only for the candidate and inputs it exercised. Changes
to code, tests, fixtures, configuration, dependency locks, validation
definitions, relevant generated artifacts, external inputs, environment, or
toolchain state invalidate the evidence they can affect. When irrelevance is not
mechanically clear, obtain fresh evidence from the affected validation.

## Required execution

Assurance sufficiency alone determines whether another execution is required.
When qualifying evidence for the exact current Candidate identity and Validation
identity settles the concrete assurance question, another execution is not
required. When it does not, execute the narrowest check that settles it.

Independent execution is required when existing evidence cannot settle a
concrete assurance question involving timing, concurrency, nondeterminism,
environment- or host-sensitive behavior, uncertain identity or provenance,
incomplete, stale, contradictory, or otherwise suspect evidence,
or a finding that needs discriminating reproduction. A documented contract or
hard rule triggers re-execution only when it requires re-execution or its
assurance question cannot otherwise be resolved. Where the assurance question
itself requires an Independent context, implementation-context execution does
not satisfy it: at least one fresh Independent review context performs the
qualifying execution. Otherwise producer role does not determine validity.

Escalate in this order:

1. inspect the existing raw evidence;
2. use static or source inspection where sufficient;
3. run the cheapest adequate targeted discriminating check; and
4. use broader execution only when the narrower check cannot answer the
   assurance question.

Timing and concurrency require the smallest reproduction that establishes the
property, not an automatic full-suite rerun. "For confidence", "to be safe",
or independently repeating an already adequate green result do not justify
another execution. One qualifying Independent execution may answer several
named assurance questions and is never required once per reviewer or stage. A
workflow-stage transition is never itself a reason to execute again.

## Repetition guardrail

Only after sufficiency is established: do not repeat materially costly
deterministic validation already covered by qualifying evidence that settles the
current assurance question. Materially costly means repeating the validation
would meaningfully add workflow latency or consume a scarce resource. Judge that
qualitatively; never consult or build a duration threshold, timing history,
telemetry-based classification, cost database, or persistent resource metadata.

This is an efficiency directive, not an assurance invariant. Violating it wastes
resources; it does not by itself make the candidate or review unsound, and it is
never a reason to skip an execution sufficiency requires. Trivially cheap checks
stay at reviewer discretion. Do not move or pre-produce validation merely to
create reusable evidence.

## Validity across stages

A later workflow stage does not by itself make deterministic evidence stale.
Qualifying evidence may satisfy later stages and final closeout while its
complete Reusable-evidence identity remains unchanged. The final blind
confirmation still independently assesses the exact clean accepted candidate
and the sufficiency of its complete direct evidence; behavior- or
evidence-changing remediation invalidates that confirmation.

Failing, stale, contradictory, incomplete, identity-invalid, or otherwise
inadequate evidence remains blocking and never reaches the repetition
guardrail. Adjudicate what failed and the evidence's bearing on the contract
before another execution; a rerun-until-green chain without adjudication cannot
erase a failure. A documented hard-rule violation remains blocking, but does
not by itself require another execution.

## Safe evidence

Evidence records never persist credential or secret values and never override
privacy, redaction, retention, or access-control constraints. Record command
structure and declared environment inputs without their sensitive values; use
an opaque safe identifier or hash when a command, argument, artifact, input, or
environment detail is sensitive. A safe provenance locator may point to
access-controlled source evidence instead of copying it. Redact or avoid
retaining secret-bearing output under the governing constraints. Unsafe or
unrecoverable evidence is non-reusable: obtain safe qualifying evidence rather
than weakening those constraints.

## Reviewer record

Keep reuse and rerun reasoning in the ordinary reviewer report. For reused
evidence, record the Reusable-evidence identity, safe provenance locator, and
fresh Independent sufficiency judgment for the named criterion or assurance
question. For an execution claimed as necessary for Independent assurance, also
name the assurance question, why existing evidence and static inspection were
insufficient, and why the execution was the narrowest adequate check. A
discretionary cheap check owes no justification record.

Do not copy raw evidence into the Run telemetry sink or create another evidence
subsystem. Raw harness transcripts and access-controlled result artifacts
remain source evidence; the reviewer report carries safe provenance and
reasoning only.

# Enforce the non-live boundary in the validation command

`./validate.sh` establishes the repository's non-live Ansible environment once
for its entire run. It exports `ANSIBLE_INVENTORY` and
`ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE` to repository-owned fixtures under `tests/`, so
lint, lifecycle launchers, pytest, and their descendants inherit the same
inputs. The fixture inventory names only the test hosts and supplies no host
addresses or SSH settings. A forgotten `connection: local` therefore cannot
resolve a managed host through production inventory. The fixture passphrase is
an inert placeholder, not a credential.

The shared regression-test helper asserts these fixture paths before it builds
the locked `uv run --locked ansible-playbook` invocation. Tests that pass their
own inventory must declare that exception explicitly; they still require the
fixture vault-password file. A plain pytest invocation does not establish this
environment, and the helper directs callers to `./validate.sh tests` when the
boundary is absent.

Per-fixture safety was rejected because hand-written `connection: local` and
individually supplied inventories make isolation depend on every test author.
Editing each playbook invocation to repeat the fixture paths was rejected as
duplicated policy that can drift. Depending on the workstation inventory and
machine-local vault passphrase was rejected because validation must not require
operator credentials. Making validation fully offline was also rejected: the
required boundary is no managed host, no vault secret, and no machine-specific
credential; public-network reads remain permitted.

This decision governs Ansible processes descended from `./validate.sh`. It does
not claim that arbitrary direct test or launcher invocations inherit the
fixtures, and it does not prohibit controlled fixture-local execution or
public-network access. It changes neither live lifecycle commands nor their
locking and wrapper safeguards.

"""Shared construction of credential-free Ansible regression invocations."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path


REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
FIXTURE_ROOT = REPO_ROOT / "tests/fixtures/ansible"
FIXTURE_INVENTORY = FIXTURE_ROOT / "inventory.yml"
FIXTURE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE = FIXTURE_ROOT / "vault-pass"
ANSIBLE_PLAYBOOK = ["uv", "run", "--locked", "ansible-playbook"]


def ansible_playbook_command(
    *arguments: str,
    supplies_own_inventory: bool = False,
) -> list[str]:
    """Return a locked playbook command under the validation fixture boundary."""
    if (
        not supplies_own_inventory
        and os.environ.get("ANSIBLE_INVENTORY") != str(FIXTURE_INVENTORY)
    ):
        raise AssertionError(
            "ANSIBLE_INVENTORY is outside the fixture environment; "
            "run this test through ./validate.sh tests"
        )
    if os.environ.get("ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE") != str(
        FIXTURE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE
    ):
        raise AssertionError(
            "ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE is outside the fixture environment; "
            "run this test through ./validate.sh tests"
        )
    return [*ANSIBLE_PLAYBOOK, *arguments]

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType

import pytest
import yaml

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

def load_helper() -> ModuleType:
    helper_path = Path(__file__).with_name("ansible_test_helper.py")
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("ansible_test_helper", helper_path)
    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def set_fixture_environment(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANSIBLE_INVENTORY", str(FIXTURE_ROOT / "inventory.yml"))
    monkeypatch.setenv(
        "ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE", str(FIXTURE_ROOT / "vault-pass")
    )


def test_constructs_locked_playbook_invocation_with_fixture_environment(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    set_fixture_environment(monkeypatch)
    helper = load_helper()

    assert helper.ansible_playbook_command("fixture.yml", "--check") == [
        "uv",
        "run",
        "--locked",
        "ansible-playbook",
        "fixture.yml",
        "--check",
    ]

    [

        ("ANSIBLE_INVENTORY", "/different/inventory.yml"),

)

# Enforce the non-live boundary in the validation command

`./validate.sh` establishes the repository's non-live Ansible environment once
for its entire run. It exports `ANSIBLE_INVENTORY` and
`ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE` to repository-owned fixtures under `tests/`, so
lint, lifecycle launchers, pytest, and their descendants inherit the same
inputs. The fixture inventory names only the test hosts and supplies no host
addresses or SSH settings. A forgotten `connection: local` therefore cannot
resolve a managed host through production inventory. The fixture passphrase is
an inert placeholder, not a credential.

The shared regression-test helper asserts these fixture paths before it builds
the locked `uv run --locked ansible-playbook` invocation. Tests that pass their
own inventory must declare that exception explicitly; they still require the
fixture vault-password file. A plain pytest invocation does not establish this
environment, and the helper directs callers to `./validate.sh tests` when the
boundary is absent.

Per-fixture safety was rejected because hand-written `connection: local` and
individually supplied inventories make isolation depend on every test author.
Editing each playbook invocation to repeat the fixture paths was rejected as
duplicated policy that can drift. Depending on the workstation inventory and
machine-local vault passphrase was rejected because validation must not require
operator credentials. Making validation fully offline was also rejected: the
required boundary is no managed host, no vault secret, and no machine-specific
credential; public-network reads remain permitted.

This decision governs Ansible processes descended from `./validate.sh`. It does
not claim that arbitrary direct test or launcher invocations inherit the
fixtures, and it does not prohibit controlled fixture-local execution or
public-network access. It changes neither live lifecycle commands nor their
locking and wrapper safeguards.

"""Shared construction of credential-free Ansible regression invocations."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path


REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
FIXTURE_ROOT = REPO_ROOT / "tests/fixtures/ansible"
FIXTURE_INVENTORY = FIXTURE_ROOT / "inventory.yml"
FIXTURE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE = FIXTURE_ROOT / "vault-pass"
ANSIBLE_PLAYBOOK = ["uv", "run", "--locked", "ansible-playbook"]


def ansible_playbook_command(
    *arguments: str,
    supplies_own_inventory: bool = False,
) -> list[str]:
    """Return a locked playbook command under the validation fixture boundary."""
    if (
        not supplies_own_inventory
        and os.environ.get("ANSIBLE_INVENTORY") != str(FIXTURE_INVENTORY)
    ):
        raise AssertionError(
            "ANSIBLE_INVENTORY is outside the fixture environment; "
            "run this test through ./validate.sh tests"
        )
    if os.environ.get("ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE") != str(
        FIXTURE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE
    ):
        raise AssertionError(
            "ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE is outside the fixture environment; "
            "run this test through ./validate.sh tests"
        )
    return [*ANSIBLE_PLAYBOOK, *arguments]

# Enforce the non-live boundary in the validation command

`./validate.sh` establishes the repository's non-live Ansible environment once
for its entire run. It exports `ANSIBLE_INVENTORY` and
`ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE` to repository-owned fixtures under `tests/`, so
lint, lifecycle launchers, pytest, and their descendants inherit the same
inputs. The fixture inventory names only the test hosts and supplies no host
addresses or SSH settings. A forgotten `connection: local` therefore cannot
resolve a managed host through production inventory. The fixture passphrase is
an inert placeholder, not a credential.

The shared regression-test helper asserts these fixture paths before it builds
the locked `uv run --locked ansible-playbook` invocation. Tests that pass their
own inventory must declare that exception explicitly; they still require the
fixture vault-password file. A plain pytest invocation does not establish this
environment, and the helper directs callers to `./validate.sh tests` when the
boundary is absent.

Per-fixture safety was rejected because hand-written `connection: local` and
individually supplied inventories make isolation depend on every test author.
Editing each playbook invocation to repeat the fixture paths was rejected as
duplicated policy that can drift. Depending on the workstation inventory and
machine-local vault passphrase was rejected because validation must not require
operator credentials. Making validation fully offline was also rejected: the
required boundary is no managed host, no vault secret, and no machine-specific
credential; public-network reads remain permitted.

This decision governs Ansible processes descended from `./validate.sh`. It does
not claim that arbitrary direct test or launcher invocations inherit the
fixtures, and it does not prohibit controlled fixture-local execution or
public-network access. It changes neither live lifecycle commands nor their
locking and wrapper safeguards.

"""Shared construction of credential-free Ansible regression invocations."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path


REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
FIXTURE_ROOT = REPO_ROOT / "tests/fixtures/ansible"
FIXTURE_INVENTORY = FIXTURE_ROOT / "inventory.yml"
FIXTURE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE = FIXTURE_ROOT / "vault-pass"
ANSIBLE_PLAYBOOK = ["uv", "run", "--locked", "ansible-playbook"]


def ansible_playbook_command(
    *arguments: str,
    supplies_own_inventory: bool = False,
) -> list[str]:
    """Return a locked playbook command under the validation fixture boundary."""
    if (
        not supplies_own_inventory
        and os.environ.get("ANSIBLE_INVENTORY") != str(FIXTURE_INVENTORY)
    ):
        raise AssertionError(
            "ANSIBLE_INVENTORY is outside the fixture environment; "
            "run this test through ./validate.sh tests"
        )
    if os.environ.get("ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE") != str(
        FIXTURE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE
    ):
        raise AssertionError(
            "ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE is outside the fixture environment; "
            "run this test through ./validate.sh tests"
        )
    return [*ANSIBLE_PLAYBOOK, *arguments]

# Enforce the non-live boundary in the validation command

`./validate.sh` establishes the repository's non-live Ansible environment once
for its entire run. It exports `ANSIBLE_INVENTORY` and
`ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE` to repository-owned fixtures under `tests/`, so
lint, lifecycle launchers, pytest, and their descendants inherit the same
inputs. The fixture inventory names only the test hosts and supplies no host
addresses or SSH settings. A forgotten `connection: local` therefore cannot
resolve a managed host through production inventory. The fixture passphrase is
an inert placeholder, not a credential.

The shared regression-test helper asserts these fixture paths before it builds
the locked `uv run --locked ansible-playbook` invocation. Tests that pass their
own inventory must declare that exception explicitly; they still require the
fixture vault-password file. A plain pytest invocation does not establish this
environment, and the helper directs callers to `./validate.sh tests` when the
boundary is absent.

Per-fixture safety was rejected because hand-written `connection: local` and
individually supplied inventories make isolation depend on every test author.
Editing each playbook invocation to repeat the fixture paths was rejected as
duplicated policy that can drift. Depending on the workstation inventory and
machine-local vault passphrase was rejected because validation must not require
operator credentials. Making validation fully offline was also rejected: the
required boundary is no managed host, no vault secret, and no machine-specific
credential; public-network reads remain permitted.

This decision governs Ansible processes descended from `./validate.sh`. It does
not claim that arbitrary direct test or launcher invocations inherit the
fixtures, and it does not prohibit controlled fixture-local execution or
public-network access. It changes neither live lifecycle commands nor their
locking and wrapper safeguards.

"""Shared construction of credential-free Ansible regression invocations."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path


REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
FIXTURE_ROOT = REPO_ROOT / "tests/fixtures/ansible"
FIXTURE_INVENTORY = FIXTURE_ROOT / "inventory.yml"
FIXTURE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE = FIXTURE_ROOT / "vault-pass"
ANSIBLE_PLAYBOOK = ["uv", "run", "--locked", "ansible-playbook"]


def ansible_playbook_command(
    *arguments: str,
    supplies_own_inventory: bool = False,
) -> list[str]:
    """Return a locked playbook command under the validation fixture boundary."""
    if (
        not supplies_own_inventory
        and os.environ.get("ANSIBLE_INVENTORY") != str(FIXTURE_INVENTORY)
    ):
        raise AssertionError(
            "ANSIBLE_INVENTORY is outside the fixture environment; "
            "run this test through ./validate.sh tests"
        )
    if os.environ.get("ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE") != str(
        FIXTURE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE
    ):
        raise AssertionError(
            "ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE is outside the fixture environment; "
            "run this test through ./validate.sh tests"
        )
    return [*ANSIBLE_PLAYBOOK, *arguments]

inventory = inventory/hosts.yml

# Ansible Inventory for Proxmox LXC Containers
# This inventory organizes hosts by resource tiers and functional groups

all:
  children:
    # API controller for Proxmox operations
    proxmox_api:
      hosts:
        proxmox_api_controller:
          ansible_connection: local
          ansible_python_interpreter: "{{ ansible_playbook_python }}"

    # LXC containers managed by Proxmox
    lxcs:
      # All managed LXC containers (for SSH-based operations after provisioning)
      # Aggregate resource tiers so LXCs only need to be listed once.
      children:
        tier_tiny:
        tier_small:
        tier_medium:
        tier_large:

    # === Resource Tier Groups ===
    # Hosts are assigned to exactly ONE resource tier based on their size needs

    tier_tiny:
      hosts:

    tier_small:
      hosts:
        auth:
        overmind:

    tier_medium:
      hosts:
        portal:
        servarr:
        # admin:
        #   Example: General media processing service

    tier_large:
      hosts:
        seedbox:
        jellyfin:
        public:
          # Example: Jellyfin media server (resource intensive)
          # Details live in inventory/host_vars/jellyfin.yml
        # Persistent remote coding workstation
        workstation:

    # === Functional Groups (Compositional) ===
    # Hosts can belong to MULTIPLE functional groups based on capabilities needed

    cap_docker:
      hosts:
        auth:
        jellyfin:
        overmind:
        portal:
        public:
        seedbox:
        servarr:
        workstation:

    cap_gpu:
      hosts:
        jellyfin:
        public:

    cap_wireguard:
      hosts:
        seedbox:
      # Placeholder for hosts needing WireGuard

[defaults]
inventory = inventory/hosts.yml
roles_path = playbooks/roles:.ansible/roles
collections_path = collections
filter_plugins = playbooks/filter_plugins
library = library
host_key_checking = False
retry_files_enabled = False
timeout = 30
stdout_callback = ansible.builtin.default
result_format = yaml
deprecation_warnings = False
bin_ansible_callbacks = True
interpreter_python = auto_silent
fact_caching = jsonfile
fact_caching_connection = .ansible/cache
fact_caching_timeout = 3600
local_tmp = .ansible/tmp
vault_password_file = ~/.ansible/vault-pass

[privilege_escalation]
# become = True  # Disabled globally - enable per-task/play as needed
become_method = sudo

[ssh_connection]
pipelining = True
control_path = .ansible/cp/%%h-%%p-%%r
ssh_args = -o IdentitiesOnly=yes
private_key_file = ~/.ansible/ssh/proxmox_lxc
---
# Ansible Inventory for Proxmox LXC Containers
# This inventory organizes hosts by resource tiers and functional groups

all:
  children:
    # API controller for Proxmox operations
    proxmox_api:
      hosts:
        proxmox_api_controller:
          ansible_connection: local
          ansible_python_interpreter: "{{ ansible_playbook_python }}"

    # LXC containers managed by Proxmox
    lxcs:
      # All managed LXC containers (for SSH-based operations after provisioning)
      # Aggregate resource tiers so LXCs only need to be listed once.
      children:
        tier_tiny:
        tier_small:
        tier_medium:
        tier_large:

    # === Resource Tier Groups ===
    # Hosts are assigned to exactly ONE resource tier based on their size needs

    tier_tiny:
      hosts:

    tier_small:
      hosts:
        auth:
        overmind:

    tier_medium:
      hosts:
        portal:
        servarr:
        # admin:
        #   Example: General media processing service

    tier_large:
      hosts:
        seedbox:
        jellyfin:
        public:
          # Example: Jellyfin media server (resource intensive)
          # Details live in inventory/host_vars/jellyfin.yml
        # Persistent remote coding workstation
        workstation:

    # === Functional Groups (Compositional) ===
    # Hosts can belong to MULTIPLE functional groups based on capabilities needed

    cap_docker:
      hosts:
        auth:
        jellyfin:
        overmind:
        portal:
        public:
        seedbox:
        servarr:
        workstation:

    cap_gpu:
      hosts:
        jellyfin:
        public:

    cap_wireguard:
      hosts:
        seedbox:
      # Placeholder for hosts needing WireGuard

[defaults]
inventory = inventory/hosts.yml
roles_path = playbooks/roles:.ansible/roles
collections_path = collections
filter_plugins = playbooks/filter_plugins
library = library
host_key_checking = False
retry_files_enabled = False
timeout = 30
stdout_callback = ansible.builtin.default
result_format = yaml
deprecation_warnings = False
bin_ansible_callbacks = True
interpreter_python = auto_silent
fact_caching = jsonfile
fact_caching_connection = .ansible/cache
fact_caching_timeout = 3600
local_tmp = .ansible/tmp
vault_password_file = ~/.ansible/vault-pass

[privilege_escalation]
# become = True  # Disabled globally - enable per-task/play as needed
become_method = sudo

[ssh_connection]
pipelining = True
control_path = .ansible/cp/%%h-%%p-%%r
ssh_args = -o IdentitiesOnly=yes
private_key_file = ~/.ansible/ssh/proxmox_lxc
---
# Ansible Inventory for Proxmox LXC Containers
# This inventory organizes hosts by resource tiers and functional groups

all:
  children:
    # API controller for Proxmox operations
    proxmox_api:
      hosts:
        proxmox_api_controller:
          ansible_connection: local
          ansible_python_interpreter: "{{ ansible_playbook_python }}"

    # LXC containers managed by Proxmox
    lxcs:
      # All managed LXC containers (for SSH-based operations after provisioning)
      # Aggregate resource tiers so LXCs only need to be listed once.
      children:
        tier_tiny:
        tier_small:
        tier_medium:
        tier_large:

    # === Resource Tier Groups ===
    # Hosts are assigned to exactly ONE resource tier based on their size needs

    tier_tiny:
      hosts:

    tier_small:
      hosts:
        auth:
        overmind:

    tier_medium:
      hosts:
        portal:
        servarr:
        # admin:
        #   Example: General media processing service

    tier_large:
      hosts:
        seedbox:
        jellyfin:
        public:
          # Example: Jellyfin media server (resource intensive)
          # Details live in inventory/host_vars/jellyfin.yml
        # Persistent remote coding workstation
        workstation:

    # === Functional Groups (Compositional) ===
    # Hosts can belong to MULTIPLE functional groups based on capabilities needed

    cap_docker:
      hosts:
        auth:
        jellyfin:
        overmind:
        portal:
        public:
        seedbox:
        servarr:
        workstation:

    cap_gpu:
      hosts:
        jellyfin:
        public:

    cap_wireguard:
      hosts:
        seedbox:
      # Placeholder for hosts needing WireGuard

# Ansible Inventory for Proxmox LXC Containers
# This inventory organizes hosts by resource tiers and functional groups

all:
  children:
    # API controller for Proxmox operations
    proxmox_api:
      hosts:
        proxmox_api_controller:
          ansible_connection: local
          ansible_python_interpreter: "{{ ansible_playbook_python }}"

    # LXC containers managed by Proxmox
    lxcs:

      # Aggregate resource tiers so LXCs only need to be listed once.
      children:
        tier_tiny:
        tier_small:
        tier_medium:
        tier_large:

    # === Resource Tier Groups ===
    # Hosts are assigned to exactly ONE resource tier based on their size needs

    tier_tiny:

    tier_small:

        overmind:

        overmind:
        portal:
        public:
        seedbox:
        servarr:
        workstation:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the LXC lifecycle regression suite: fast feedback or full completion.

Thin runner only: it selects, launches, and reports the existing standalone
launchers. Every lifecycle scenario, input, and assertion stays in the
Ansible fixtures those launchers execute (see ADR 0007).

Fast path (default) — routine agent iteration:
  the semantic lifecycle facade matrix (planning, lifecycle intent,
  persistent destructive policy, result classification, controlled
  execution outcomes) plus the targeted lifecycle planning barrier.
Full path (--full) — completion checks before handoff:
  everything the fast path covers, plus the remaining lifecycle seams,
  including slow host-configuration idempotence sequencing and the real
  role-composition wiring regression.
Targeted path (--only FILENAME, repeatable) — focused remediation:
  registered launchers run sequentially in the supplied order. Add
  --fail-fast to stop scheduling selected launchers after the first failure.
  With --full, fail-fast still lets the concurrent fast launchers finish,
  then schedules no new launcher after a failure.

Both paths use controlled observations only: no live Proxmox, no vault
secrets, no machine-specific credentials.

Lifecycle planning keeps compilation and semantic plan construction in
independently scheduled Ansible plays. Fleet preflight and the all-target
planning barrier run only after their preceding target-local phase completes;
production execution remains linear. This preserves the full Ansible-native
scenario matrix while avoiding target-local planner task waves at the
targeted-set coordination seams (issue #44).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Sequence


TESTS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPO_ROOT = TESTS.parents[1]

# Both fast launchers are internally parallel and fully isolated (per-run
# temp state directories), so the fast path runs them concurrently.
FAST_SCRIPTS = (
    "test_lxc_lifecycle_decision.py",
    "test_lxc_lifecycle_planning_barrier.py",
)

# The rest of the lifecycle set runs sequentially: the host-configuration
# idempotence sequence and wiring regression are heavyweight, and sequential
# execution keeps their timing and failure attribution predictable.
FULL_ONLY_SCRIPTS = (
    "test_lifecycle_run_lock.py",
    "test_lxc_lifecycle_invalid_state.py",
    "test_lxc_lifecycle_guest_bootstrap_contract.py",
    "test_lxc_spec_contract.py",
    "test_lxc_spec_invalid_guest_bootstrap.py",
    "test_lxc_spec_layer_merge.py",
    "test_proxmox_lxc_provision_contract.py",
    "test_proxmox_lxc_lifecycle_configure_check_mode_absent.py",
    "test_proxmox_lxc_lifecycle_observation_status.py",
    "test_lxc_manual_ssh_recovery.py",
    "test_lxc_ssh_key_injector_identity_mismatch.py",
    "test_lxc_fleet_preflight.py",
    "test_proxmox_lxc_host_config_check_mode_missing_config.py",
    "test_proxmox_lxc_host_config_observation_failure.py",
    "test_proxmox_lxc_host_config_readiness_deadline.py",
    "test_lxc_docker_runtime_daemon_options.py",
    "test_lxc_nvidia_runtime_repository.py",
    "test_lxc_lifecycle_wiring.py",
    "test_proxmox_lxc_host_config_result.py",
    "test_hawser_standard_remote_default.py",
    "test_fixture_fact_cache_isolation.py",
)
REGISTERED_SCRIPTS = FAST_SCRIPTS + FULL_ONLY_SCRIPTS

LauncherResult = tuple[str, int, float, str]
Launcher = Callable[[str], LauncherResult]


def run_script(script: str) -> tuple[str, int, float, str]:
    start = time.monotonic()
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(TESTS / script)],
        cwd=REPO_ROOT,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    wall = time.monotonic() - start
    return script, proc.returncode, wall, f"{proc.stdout}\n{proc.stderr}"


def report(result: tuple[str, int, float, str]) -> bool:
    script, returncode, wall, output = result
    status = "PASS" if returncode == 0 else "FAIL"
    print(f"{status}  {script}  ({wall:.1f}s)", flush=True)
    if returncode != 0:
        print(output, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    return returncode == 0


def run_regressions(
    *,
    full: bool,
    fail_fast: bool = False,
    only: Sequence[str] = (),
    launcher: Launcher = run_script,
) -> int:
    failed = []
    launched = 0
    if only:
        for script in only:
            launched += 1
            if not report(launcher(script)):
                failed.append(script)
                if fail_fast:
                    break
        if failed:
            print(f"failed: {', '.join(failed)}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print(f"ok: targeted lifecycle regression set passed ({launched} launchers)")
        return 0

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(FAST_SCRIPTS)) as executor:
        for result in executor.map(launcher, FAST_SCRIPTS):
            launched += 1
            if not report(result):
                failed.append(result[0])
    if failed and fail_fast:
        print(f"failed: {', '.join(failed)}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if full:
        for script in FULL_ONLY_SCRIPTS:
            launched += 1
            if not report(launcher(script)):
                failed.append(script)
                if fail_fast:
                    break

    if failed:
        print(f"failed: {', '.join(failed)}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    label = "full lifecycle regression set" if full else "fast lifecycle feedback path"
    print(f"ok: {label} passed ({launched} launchers)")
    return 0


def main(
    argv: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    *,
    launcher: Launcher = run_script,
) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--full",
        action="store_true",
        help="run the complete lifecycle regression set, not just fast feedback",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--only",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        metavar="FILENAME",
        help="run only this registered launcher (repeatable)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--fail-fast",
        action="store_true",
        help="stop scheduling new launchers after a failure",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.only and args.full:
        parser.error("--only cannot be combined with --full")
    unknown_scripts = [script for script in args.only if script not in REGISTERED_SCRIPTS]
    if unknown_scripts:
        parser.error(
            f"unknown lifecycle launcher: {unknown_scripts[0]}; "
            f"registered launchers: {', '.join(REGISTERED_SCRIPTS)}"
        )

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="lxc-lifecycle-fixtures-") as temp_dir:
        temp_root = Path(temp_dir)
        # ansible.cfg names a vault password file that must exist, but the
        # fixtures decrypt nothing: a placeholder keeps the run credential-free.
        vault_placeholder = temp_root / "vault-pass"
        vault_placeholder.write_text(
            "unused-fixture-placeholder\n", encoding="utf-8"
        )
        fixture_inventory = temp_root / "inventory.ini"
        fixture_inventory.write_text(
            "[local]\nlocalhost ansible_connection=local\n", encoding="utf-8"
        )
        previous_vault_password_file = os.environ.get("ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE")
        previous_inventory = os.environ.get("ANSIBLE_INVENTORY")
        previous_cache_plugin_connection = os.environ.get(
            "ANSIBLE_CACHE_PLUGIN_CONNECTION"
        )
        os.environ["ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE"] = str(vault_placeholder)
        os.environ["ANSIBLE_INVENTORY"] = str(fixture_inventory)
        # Fixtures add fake hosts (e.g. s1_portal) that fact caching would
        # otherwise persist for up to the production TTL. Redirect the jsonfile
        # cache per run instead of forcing memory so within-run caching
        # semantics stay production-like while .ansible/cache stays untouched
        # (issue #89).
        os.environ["ANSIBLE_CACHE_PLUGIN_CONNECTION"] = str(temp_root / "fact-cache")
        try:
            return run_regressions(
                full=args.full,
                fail_fast=args.fail_fast,
                only=args.only,
                launcher=launcher,
            )
        finally:
            if previous_vault_password_file is None:
                os.environ.pop("ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE", None)
            else:
                os.environ["ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE"] = previous_vault_password_file
            if previous_inventory is None:
                os.environ.pop("ANSIBLE_INVENTORY", None)
            else:
                os.environ["ANSIBLE_INVENTORY"] = previous_inventory
            if previous_cache_plugin_connection is None:
                os.environ.pop("ANSIBLE_CACHE_PLUGIN_CONNECTION", None)
            else:
                os.environ["ANSIBLE_CACHE_PLUGIN_CONNECTION"] = (
                    previous_cache_plugin_connection
                )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

REGISTERED_SCRIPTS = FAST_SCRIPTS + FULL_ONLY_SCRIPTS

LauncherResult = tuple[str, int, float, str]
Launcher = Callable[[str], LauncherResult]


def run_script(script: str) -> tuple[str, int, float, str]:
    start = time.monotonic()
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, str(TESTS / script)],
        cwd=REPO_ROOT,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    wall = time.monotonic() - start
    return script, proc.returncode, wall, f"{proc.stdout}\n{proc.stderr}"


def report(result: tuple[str, int, float, str]) -> bool:
    script, returncode, wall, output = result
    status = "PASS" if returncode == 0 else "FAIL"
    print(f"{status}  {script}  ({wall:.1f}s)", flush=True)
    if returncode != 0:
        print(output, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    return returncode == 0


def run_regressions(
    *,
    full: bool,
    fail_fast: bool = False,
    only: Sequence[str] = (),
    launcher: Launcher = run_script,
) -> int:
    failed = []
    launched = 0
    if only:
        for script in only:
            launched += 1
            if not report(launcher(script)):
                failed.append(script)
                if fail_fast:
                    break
        if failed:
            print(f"failed: {', '.join(failed)}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print(f"ok: targeted lifecycle regression set passed ({launched} launchers)")
        return 0

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(FAST_SCRIPTS)) as executor:
        for result in executor.map(launcher, FAST_SCRIPTS):
            launched += 1
            if not report(result):
                failed.append(result[0])
    if failed and fail_fast:
        print(f"failed: {', '.join(failed)}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if full:
        for script in FULL_ONLY_SCRIPTS:
            launched += 1
            if not report(launcher(script)):
                failed.append(script)
                if fail_fast:
                    break

    if failed:
        print(f"failed: {', '.join(failed)}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    label = "full lifecycle regression set" if full else "fast lifecycle feedback path"
    print(f"ok: {label} passed ({launched} launchers)")
    return 0


def main(
    argv: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    *,
    launcher: Launcher = run_script,
) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--full",
        action="store_true",
        help="run the complete lifecycle regression set, not just fast feedback",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--only",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        metavar="FILENAME",
        help="run only this registered launcher (repeatable)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--fail-fast",
        action="store_true",
        help="stop scheduling new launchers after a failure",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.only and args.full:
        parser.error("--only cannot be combined with --full")
    unknown_scripts = [script for script in args.only if script not in REGISTERED_SCRIPTS]
    if unknown_scripts:
        parser.error(
            f"unknown lifecycle launcher: {unknown_scripts[0]}; "
            f"registered launchers: {', '.join(REGISTERED_SCRIPTS)}"
        )

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="lxc-lifecycle-fixtures-") as temp_dir:
        temp_root = Path(temp_dir)
        # ansible.cfg names a vault password file that must exist, but the
        # fixtures decrypt nothing: a placeholder keeps the run credential-free.
        vault_placeholder = temp_root / "vault-pass"
        vault_placeholder.write_text(
            "unused-fixture-placeholder\n", encoding="utf-8"
        )
        fixture_inventory = temp_root / "inventory.ini"
        fixture_inventory.write_text(
            "[local]\nlocalhost ansible_connection=local\n", encoding="utf-8"
        )
        previous_vault_password_file = os.environ.get("ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE")
        previous_inventory = os.environ.get("ANSIBLE_INVENTORY")
        previous_cache_plugin_connection = os.environ.get(
            "ANSIBLE_CACHE_PLUGIN_CONNECTION"
        )
        os.environ["ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE"] = str(vault_placeholder)
        os.environ["ANSIBLE_INVENTORY"] = str(fixture_inventory)
        # Fixtures add fake hosts (e.g. s1_portal) that fact caching would
        # otherwise persist for up to the production TTL. Redirect the jsonfile
        # cache per run instead of forcing memory so within-run caching
        # semantics stay production-like while .ansible/cache stays untouched
        # (issue #89).
        os.environ["ANSIBLE_CACHE_PLUGIN_CONNECTION"] = str(temp_root / "fact-cache")
        try:
            return run_regressions(
                full=args.full,
                fail_fast=args.fail_fast,
                only=args.only,
                launcher=launcher,
            )
        finally:
            if previous_vault_password_file is None:
                os.environ.pop("ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE", None)
            else:
                os.environ["ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE"] = previous_vault_password_file
            if previous_inventory is None:
                os.environ.pop("ANSIBLE_INVENTORY", None)
            else:
                os.environ["ANSIBLE_INVENTORY"] = previous_inventory
            if previous_cache_plugin_connection is None:
                os.environ.pop("ANSIBLE_CACHE_PLUGIN_CONNECTION", None)
            else:
                os.environ["ANSIBLE_CACHE_PLUGIN_CONNECTION"] = (
                    previous_cache_plugin_connection
                )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

     1	# Enforce the non-live boundary in the validation command
     2	
     3	`./validate.sh` establishes the repository's non-live Ansible environment once
     4	for its entire run. It exports `ANSIBLE_INVENTORY` and
     5	`ANSIBLE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE` to repository-owned fixtures under `tests/`, so
     6	lint, lifecycle launchers, pytest, and their descendants inherit the same
     7	inputs. The fixture inventory names only the test hosts and supplies no host
     8	addresses or SSH settings. A forgotten `connection: local` therefore cannot
     9	resolve a managed host through production inventory. The fixture passphrase is
    10	an inert placeholder, not a credential.
    11	
    12	The shared regression-test helper asserts these fixture paths before it builds
    13	the locked `uv run --locked ansible-playbook` invocation. Tests that pass their
    14	own inventory must declare that exception explicitly; they still require the
    15	fixture vault-password file. A plain pytest invocation does not establish this
    16	environment, and the helper directs callers to `./validate.sh tests` when the
    17	boundary is absent.
    18	
    19	Per-fixture safety was rejected because hand-written `connection: local` and
    20	individually supplied inventories make isolation depend on every test author.
    21	Editing each playbook invocation to repeat the fixture paths was rejected as
    22	duplicated policy that can drift. Depending on the workstation inventory and
    23	machine-local vault passphrase was rejected because validation must not require
    24	operator credentials. Making validation fully offline was also rejected: the
    25	required boundary is no managed host, no vault secret, and no machine-specific
    26	credential; public-network reads remain permitted.
    27	
    28	This decision governs Ansible processes descended from `./validate.sh`. It does
    29	not claim that arbitrary direct test or launcher invocations inherit the
    30	fixtures, and it does not prohibit controlled fixture-local execution or
    31	public-network access. It changes neither live lifecycle commands nor their
    32	locking and wrapper safeguards.

     4	
     5	import os
     6	from pathlib import Path

     9	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    10	FIXTURE_ROOT = REPO_ROOT / "tests/fixtures/ansible"
    11	FIXTURE_INVENTORY = FIXTURE_ROOT / "inventory.yml"
    12	FIXTURE_VAULT_PASSWORD_FILE = FIXTURE_ROOT / "vault-pass"

# Keep LXC lifecycle policy in Ansible

LXC contract compilation, semantic lifecycle planning, and execution remain Ansible-native so the repository retains one architectural center for infrastructure convergence. Lifecycle scenarios, inputs, semantic assertions, and decisions therefore stay in Ansible. Python may select, schedule, launch, report, and test the orchestration of the standalone lifecycle regression launchers, but it may not reimplement lifecycle policy or use Python assertions as a substitute for Ansible-native semantic coverage.

The semantic lifecycle plan is the stable interface and test surface; moving core policy into Python requires demonstrated pressure such as repeated type-related bugs, duplicated decisions, or an unmanageable Ansible scenario matrix rather than anticipated future growth.
